CrediX Finance, a Sonic lending protocol, was drained of $4.5M in August 2025 after an attacker gained core admin privileges. The exploiter minted unbacked collateral, borrowed from pools, and bridged assets to Ethereum. The team later vanished, raising strong exit scam suspicions. The attack was enabled by governance failure: a single address was assigned multiple high-impact admin roles (including minting and bridge privileges) via the protocol's ACLManager, with no effective multisig or timelock protections. This allowed unbacked collateral to be minted and used to drain liquidity pools. There is no evidence of a direct smart contract bug; the failure was in unchecked admin controls.
